Popular environmental knowledge is diverse and syncretic. It takes multiple forms of expertise and brings them down to size. This is not a one-way street, however. Individuals, including scientists, politicians, and activists, apply their eclectic perspectives in forming projects of nature-making.
原页 113
通俗环境知识是多样且混合的。它采用多种专业知识形式，并把它们缩小到可理解的尺度。然而，这并不是一条单行道。个人，包括科学家、政治家和活动家，在形成自然制造项目时运用他们兼收并蓄的视角。
原页 113

It makes no sense to search for a singular “Indonesian” environmental knowledge or one divided neatly into ethnic groups or religions. Instead, we might begin by identifying distinctive confluences of knowledge, as well as the nodes of practice and discourse informed by these confluences.
原页 113
寻找一种单一的“印尼”环境知识，或一种按族群或宗教整齐划分的知识，是没有意义的。相反，我们也许可以首先识别知识的不同汇流，以及受这些汇流影响的实践与话语节点。
原页 113

1997. President Suharto is still in power, but the New Order regime is beginning to unravel. Oppositional voices are growing louder even in the provinces. In South Kalimantan, these voices are moral and religious in their tone. They raise a new question about the environment: What if nature is a moral question?
原页 113
1997年。苏哈托总统仍在掌权，但新秩序政权开始瓦解。即使在各省，反对声音也越来越响亮。在南加里曼丹，这些声音在语调上是道德和宗教的。它们提出了一个关于环境的新问题：如果自然是一个道德问题呢？

Late one night, in a provincial town in South Kalimantan, the guests had finally left the mulut gathering, and I found myself in focused conversation with the host, a batik merchant, who was smoking a cigarette.

“People say that smoking causes sickness; but actually it is the human heart [hati] that causes sickness. If you have only good deeds, cigarettes—or any foods—won’t harm you. The important thing is what is in your heart. It is better to associate with thieves than with someone whose speech is different than his heart.

“Everything that a person does should have a use for others. Otherwise people are more stupid than rocks, more stupid than the sun, moon, and stars. How can people be as stupid as dead matter? God made humans to guard the conservation of the earth. But this can only be done by recognizing that people do not live alone, like Robinson Crusoe. We live in a world connected with others, and everything we do must be of use to others. It is useless to do meditation exercises alone on mountains or on a rock in the ocean: What use does this have for others? Everything we do must have use, and this can only be gained by losing one’s ego, one’s ‘I.’ We don’t need to hate others, to be jealous, to be angry. Our sense of ego is what causes ruin in the world.

“People are worried about climate change. But it’s not industry that causes climate change. It’s the doing of people. Every action of a person causes a wave, and these waves meet and reverberate in the atmosphere. A good action causes a ray of brightness; a bad action causes a dark ray [cehaya gelap]. If there are many dark rays, the sunshine will not come through.

“There are many kinds of rays: ultraviolet; alpha; beta; x-rays. (They call them ‘x-rays’ because they don’t understand them; so they say ‘x.’ Did you know this?) There are other rays caused by human conduct. These influence the world.

“There is electricity in the human body. It’s not the same as electricity in the world, which lights the lamps. But how could a child form in the womb before it has received a soul? Only because of electricity. The man has positive electricity. The woman has negative electricity. The woman has elements of the earth; the man has elements of the heavens. These come together and a child is made from earth and sky, positive and negative electricity.

“Human actions affect atomic particles. There are two kinds of atomic particles: those under control, and those out of control. A bad heart makes things out of control. A good heart makes things under control. This is where science and religion meet. It’s no different from what foreign scientists say, but they haven’t given these things enough attention.

“God made the elements of the earth to stabilize the earth. There is iron, gold, silver, oil, coal: All give the earth stability. When people mine these until one element is gone, there will be no more stability to the crust of the earth. Inside the earth, lava flows in a more and more liquid form, and deep inside there is gas. It is very hot, perhaps 6,000 degrees or more. If the stability of the crust of the earth is disturbed, it will sink into the liquid and gas below. If you take out any of the elements of the earth until one is gone, the stability will be lost.
“Can you take this in, Anna?

“Every religion, whether Islam, Christianity, Judaism, or Buddhism, teaches us the effects of our hearts on our own world. Why do we pray? It’s not just to praise God. Our prayers come back to us humans, to make us conscious of ourselves. That is the promise of prayer, to raise self-consciousness [kesadaran diri]. The conscience [hati kecil] has its own influence on the world, different than thoughts. For example, sometimes you have a feeling you shouldn’t travel; you travel anyway and meet an accident. It is the conscience that should guide our actions. This is only possible by uniting microcosm and macrocosm, and by losing the sense of self.

“Have you ever seen water flow up? It always flows down. When you drop a rock, does it ever go upwards? It always falls to the ground. This is the way of nature. People are greedy and don’t accept this.”
深夜，在南加里曼丹一个地方城镇，客人终于离开了 mulut 聚会，我发现自己与主人——一位正在抽烟的蜡染商人——进行着专注的交谈。
“人们说吸烟导致疾病；但实际上是人心（hati）导致疾病。如果你只有善行，香烟——或任何食物——都不会伤害你。重要的是你心里有什么。与其和说话与心不一的人交往，不如和小偷交往。

“一个人所做的一切都应该对他人有用。否则人比石头还愚蠢，比太阳、月亮和星星还愚蠢。人怎么能像死物质一样愚蠢？上帝造人是为了守护和保全大地。但这只有通过认识到人不是像鲁滨逊·克鲁索那样独自生活才能做到。我们生活在一个与他人相连的世界中，我们所做的一切都必须对他人有用。独自在山上或海中的岩石上冥想是没用的：这对他人有什么用处？我们所做的一切都必须有用，而这只有通过失去自我、失去‘我’才能获得。我们不需要恨别人、嫉妒、愤怒。我们的自我感是造成世界毁灭的原因。
“人们担心气候变化。但造成气候变化的不是工业。是人的所作所为。一个人的每一个行动都会引起波，这些波在大气中相遇并回响。善行产生一束明亮射线；恶行产生一道暗射线（cehaya gelap）。如果暗射线很多，阳光就透不过来。
“射线有很多种：紫外线；阿尔法射线；贝塔射线；X射线。（他们称之为‘X射线’是因为他们不理解它；所以他们说‘X’。你知道这个吗？）还有人类行为引起的其他射线。这些影响世界。
“人体内有电。它不同于世界上点亮灯的电。但一个孩子在获得灵魂之前，怎么能在子宫里形成？只因为电。男人有正电。女人有负电。女人有土的元素；男人有天的元素。这些结合在一起，孩子由土与天空、正电与负电造成。
“人类行为影响原子粒子。原子粒子有两种：受控的和失控的。坏心使事物失控。好心使事物受控。这就是科学与宗教相遇的地方。这与外国科学家所说的没有不同，只是他们没有给予这些事情足够的关注。
“上帝创造地球的元素来稳定地球。有铁、金、银、石油、煤：所有这些都给地球稳定。当人们开采这些，直到某种元素消失，地壳将不再有稳定性。地球内部，熔岩以越来越液态的形式流动，深处有气体。那里非常热，也许6000度或更高。如果地壳的稳定性受到扰动，它将沉入下面的液体和气体。如果你取出地球的任何元素，直到一种消失，稳定性就会丧失。
“你能接受这些吗，安娜？

“每一种宗教，无论是伊斯兰教、基督教、犹太教还是佛教，都教导我们心对我们自己世界的影响。我们为什么祈祷？不只是为了赞美上帝。我们的祈祷回到我们人类身上，使我们意识到自己。这就是祈祷的承诺，提升自我意识（kesadaran diri）。良心（hati kecil）对世界有自己的影响，不同于思想。例如，有时你有种感觉不应该旅行；你还是旅行了，遇到了事故。应该指导我们行动的是良心。这只有通过统一微观宇宙与宏观宇宙、通过失去自我感才有可能。
“你见过水向上流吗？它总是向下流。当你丢下一块石头，它会向上吗？它总是落到地上。这是自然之道。人们贪婪，不接受这一点。”
原页 115

Ahmad is an educated man. He spends most of his days seated at his stall at the market unfolding colorful sarongs for customers and supervising the young men who help him show his cloths. But he has been to college, and he has kept up particularly with natural science, philosophy, and religion. I have known him for a long time, and we often have these kinds of conversations when I see him. He knows me as a fellow scholastic, with whom he can share serious thoughts.
原页 115
艾哈迈德是个受过教育的人。他大多数日子坐在市场摊位上，为顾客展开色彩鲜艳的纱笼，并监督帮他展示布料的年轻人。但他上过大学，尤其关注自然科学、哲学和宗教。我认识他很久了，每次见到他，我们常有这类对话。他把我当作一位学者同侪，可以与之分享严肃想法。
原页 115
I didn’t want to be a merchant. I wanted to study when I was still a bachelor. I studied so much my father worried I would go crazy, so he married me off.

我不想做商人。我还是单身时想学习。我学得太用功，父亲担心我会发疯，就让我结了婚。

Ahmad reads voraciously. Most of what is locally available are pamphlets on various aspects of Islamic faith. He pulls these together with his thoughts on science to forge a synthesis between the world as known by science and as known by religion.
原页 115
艾哈迈德博览群书。当地可得到的大部分是关于伊斯兰信仰各方面的小册子。他把这些与自己对科学的思考结合起来，在科学所知的世界与宗教所知的世界之间锻造一种综合。
原页 115

The Koran speaks of the seven layers of the earth and the seven layers of the heavens. Science has only begun to know the first layers. It is all written in the Koran, but we have yet to know about these things. For example, it will be found that there are fourteen planets, seven we know and seven beyond Pluto that we don’t yet know.
原页 115
《古兰经》谈到地球的七层和天的七层。科学才刚刚开始认识最初的几层。这一切都写在《古兰经》里，但我们还没有认识这些事情。例如，人们会发现有十四颗行星，七颗我们知道，七颗在冥王星之外我们尚不知道。
原页 115

The synthesis he offers is distinctive, but it does not make use of only local materials. Ahmad mentions Robinson Crusoe; when he talks about philosophy, he refers to Aristotle, Descartes, Hobbes, and Kant. After the conversation above, he recommended a book to me, which turned out to be the Indonesian translation of a treatise published by the State University of New York, called The Tao of Islam (Murata 1992). Ahmad is especially drawn to spiritual forms of understanding through which to blend religion and science.
原页 115
他提供的综合很独特，但并不只使用地方材料。艾哈迈德提到鲁滨逊·克鲁索；谈到哲学时，他提到亚里士多德、笛卡尔、霍布斯和康德。上述对话之后，他向我推荐了一本书，结果是纽约州立大学出版社出版的一部论著的印尼文译本，名为《伊斯兰之道》（The Tao of Islam）（Murata 1992）。艾哈迈德尤其被精神性的理解形式所吸引，借此融合宗教与科学。

Through this distinctive cosmopolitanism, he has put together a philosophy of nature—and, indeed, of nature conservation.
原页 116
通过这种独特的世界主义，他拼合出一种自然哲学——实际上也是一种自然保护哲学。

It never used to be so hot as this. This is probably due to cutting down the trees. Every movement has a sound. Now there are more sounds than movements, because of television, radio, chain saws, motorboats, and the like. The atmosphere is like a container; sounds are not lost from it. They travel from one place to another creating new influences. The relation between the earth and the sun changes as a result.
原页 116
以前从没这么热过。这大概是因为砍树。每个运动都有声音。现在声音比运动多，因为电视、收音机、链锯、摩托艇等等。大气就像一个容器；声音不会从中消失。它们从一个地方传到另一个地方，创造新的影响。地球与太阳的关系因此改变。
原页 116

Ahmad’s discussion of nature conservation would not be recognized by environmental activists in South Kalimantan as their kind of talk; they would consider him countrified, quirky, and out of touch. He does not share their access to international circuits of environmental information and action; he does not use their rhetoric. Yet his ideas are consonant in many ways with the spirit of engaged intellectual discussion of nature in South Kalimantan. Like better recognized intellectuals, Ahmad looks for nature in the confluence between modern science and Islamic precept. Ahmad does not think that science and religion offer alternate ways of approaching nature. There is no divide between faith and reason, as in Western tradition. Instead, modern science and Islam reveal the same truth. Apparent divergences are only temporary misunderstandings that will disappear as we learn more about God’s world. The challenge of learning is to accept this.
原页 116

艾哈迈德关于自然保护的讨论，不会被南加里曼丹的环保活动家认作他们那类谈话；他们会认为他土气、古怪、脱离时代。他不享有他们进入国际环境信息与行动渠道的机会；他不使用他们的修辞。然而，他的想法在许多方面与南加里曼丹介入现实的知识分子关于自然的讨论的精神一致。像更受认可的知识分子一样，艾哈迈德在现代科学与伊斯兰教义的交汇处寻找自然。艾哈迈德不认为科学与宗教提供接近自然的替代方式。这里不存在西方传统中那种信仰与理性之间的分界。相反，现代科学与伊斯兰教揭示同一个真理。表面分歧只是暂时的误解，随着我们对上帝世界了解更多就会消失。学习的挑战就是接受这一点。

Ahmad identifies the route to understanding nature as proceeding through personal spiritual experience, as well as ethical choice for right conduct. The microcosm of one’s personal awareness must be brought into alignment with the macrocosm of the universe. Personal self-interest must be discarded so that a larger “global” understanding can enter one’s consciousness. Although the personal character of awareness is essential in Ahmad’s discussion, this is not the same personal spirituality that I heard about from the Javanese student nature lovers I describe in the next chapter. For cosmopolitan Javanese youth, personal spirituality is a break from the rigidity of established values; it is a world of insight that comes directly from mysterious sources, bypassing orthodox opinion. It recognizes equal ties to U.S. New Age spirituality, Islamic religiosity, and Javanese mysticism. In contrast, Ahmad’s personal spirituality opens the self to the power of truth in religion and science. It does not require nonconformism; indeed, it rejects the goal of self-differentiation as self-aggrandizement. Instead of egotistically searching out mysteries, we must each ask ourselves about our willingness to accept God’s universe, just as Ahmad asked me: “Can you take this in?”

Authoritative texts are an important way to open one’s understanding of God’s universe. These include the Koran and its interpretations, as well as the texts of modern science. Reading and rereading these texts, one can lose self-interest and approach the truth. This is the point of scholarship, whether religious or scientific.

艾哈迈德认为，理解自然的道路要通过个人精神体验，以及对正确行为的伦理选择。个人意识的微观宇宙必须与宇宙的宏观宇宙对齐。个人私利必须被抛弃，以便更大的“全球”理解进入意识。虽然意识的个人性在艾哈迈德的讨论中至关重要，这与我下一章描述的爪哇学生自然爱好者告诉我的个人灵性并不相同。对世界主义的爪哇青年来说，个人灵性是摆脱既定价值僵化的一种突破；它是一个直接来自神秘来源的洞见世界，绕过正统意见。它承认与美国新时代灵性、伊斯兰宗教性和爪哇神秘主义的平等联系。相比之下，艾哈迈德的个人灵性向宗教与科学中的真理力量敞开自我。它不要求人们离经叛道；事实上，它拒绝自我区分的目标，视之为自我膨胀。与其自我中心地寻找神秘，我们必须各自问自己是否愿意接受上帝的宇宙，就像艾哈迈德问我：“你能接受这些吗？”
权威文本是打开对上帝宇宙理解的重要方式。这些包括《古兰经》及其解释，以及现代科学的文本。阅读和重读这些文本，人可以失去私利并接近真理。这就是学术的要义，无论是宗教还是科学。
原页 117

These assumptions frame intellectual discussion of the big questions of nature and society in South Kalimantan. In the mid-1990s, activists, professionals, and professors developed these frames together with ordinary ethical men. The environment, along with democracy and justice, emerged as an object at the confluence of religion and science. The management of the relationship of humans and nature was best considered through the interpretation of authoritative texts, and the goal was to raise ethical standards of behavior.
原页 117
这些假设构成了南加里曼丹关于自然与社会大问题的知识讨论框架。20世纪90年代中期，活动家、专业人士和教授与讲求伦理的普通男性一起发展这些框架。环境，连同民主与正义，作为宗教与科学交汇处的对象出现。人与自然关系的管理最好通过解释权威文本来考虑，目标是提高行为的伦理标准。
原页 117
In the mid-1990s, Professor N. was a teacher, a journalist, and a political activist in the provincial capital.

He was the founder of an organization that specialized in issues of law and the environment. Unostentatious and sociable, he was a popular teacher, and many of his students followed him into his NGO to pursue the interests he sparked in them concerning democracy and governance. “Usman” also wrote essays for the local newspaper. He became a political commentator in authoritarian times; he was brave but cautious in his opinions. In public seminars, he raised sharp and pressing questions. But he also quickly withdrew them if they attracted too much attention.
原页 117
20世纪90年代中期，N教授是省会的一名教师、记者和政治活动家。
他创立了一个专门处理法律与环境问题的组织。他不张扬，善于交际，是一位受欢迎的老师，许多学生跟随他进入他的非政府组织，追求他激发起的对民主与治理的兴趣。“乌斯曼”还为当地报纸写文章。他在威权时代成为政治评论员；他的观点勇敢而谨慎。在公开研讨会上，他提出尖锐而紧迫的问题。但如果这些问题引起太多注意，他也会很快收回。
原页 117

Usman did not come to environmental issues as a nature lover; he was a student activist. When we spoke in 1997, he admitted to me good-naturedly that he formed his NGO first and then looked around for some issues for it to address; he picked the environment because he thought he could make a difference with this issue, given its high public profile. His wife, however, was once a student nature lover. She had been an avid rock climber when they met. Now, he chuckled, their one-year-old baby loves to play with ropes. He forbids his wife to climb, he explained solicitously; it is too dangerous for women. Rock climbing is a better sport for men. They went camping, once, but the baby was angry and cried.
原页 117

乌斯曼并非作为自然爱好者进入环境议题；他曾是学生活动家。1997年我们交谈时，他和气地向我承认，他先成立了自己的非政府组织，然后才四处寻找一些议题让它处理；他选择了环境，因为他认为鉴于该议题的高公众关注度，他可以有所作为。然而，他的妻子曾是学生自然爱好者。他们相识时，她是个热心的攀岩者。现在，他咯咯笑着说，他们一岁的宝宝喜欢玩绳子。他体贴地解释说，他禁止妻子攀岩；这对女人太危险。攀岩是更适合男人的运动。他们去露营过一次，但宝宝生气了，哭个不停。

After inviting me to his house and introducing me to his reticent, pious, and polite wife, who, indeed, it seemed, had been domesticated by marriage, Usman opened the big notebooks that held the manuscripts of the essays he had written for the newspaper. The bulk of what he showed me were articles on environmental law. But I could see, interlaced with them, many articles on religion. He explained that these had become his two passions—each at the heart of political action. Each structured his approach to both scholarship and politics: the laws of God and the laws of society.
在邀请我去他家，并把我介绍给他沉默、虔诚、礼貌的妻子——她确实看起来已被婚姻驯化——之后，乌斯曼打开大笔记本，里面是他为报纸写的文章手稿。他给我看的大部分是关于环境法的文章。但我能看到，与它们交织的还有许多关于宗教的文章。他解释说，这些已成为他的两大热情——各自处于政治行动的核心。每一个都塑造了他对学术和政治的方法：上帝的法则与社会的法则。
原页 118

Law was at the center of Usman’s moral world. He had written at least one essay about the nature of law itself. Law, he argues, is at the heart of our ability to choose right conduct. From law, cultural norms emerge, which help us negotiate the tension between ideals and realities. Laws are norms that challenge people to reach their ideals, within cultural standards. The abstract and systemic nature of law makes it available as a system of guidelines for human behavior. Through the careful study of law, it is possible to raise awareness about environmental and theological issues. Through awareness, people may make better choices.

Law defines things. It offers a rational frame. What is the role of humanity according to the Koran? Usman asks in one essay. His answer begins with the distinction between humans and other creatures. Like other living beings, humans sustain themselves, obtain foods, and reproduce; like other animals, humans have senses and desires; but, among all beings, only humans have the power to reason, and thus to contribute to shaping the future they would like. Humans are responsible to make their own fate. He quotes the Koran about human privilege: “And He made you to control the earth...” and reminds us of the human fall from grace. God taught Adam the names of all things, and thus raised him above even the angels. Now humans have the responsibility for themselves and for the natural world. Humans can choose God, or they face a bleak future. “God explains this matter in the Koran: ‘Whoever is unwilling to remember Me, surely he will face a barren life and in the afterlife will be assembled with the blind.”

What did “nature” look like here? What kinds of environmental activism were possible in this space of reform and piety? South Kalimantan environmentalism in the late New Order flourished in a moral space that distinguished it from other times and places. For the activists I met, justice and right-doing were the priority. Biocentric nature conservation was promoted by several bureaus and organizations, but it was not a popular social cause. Pollution was an important issue for government-corporate negotiations, but it did not move young activists. Ethical behavior was the key political issue.

Political change can sometimes be quite sudden. A few years later, the spirit of activism felt quite different: with the fall of the New Order and the rise of a more open national politics, secular and pluralistic stances became possible (see chapter 6). There have also been continuities. Banjar environmental activists continue to struggle within the moral economy of regional social justice. Yet the rapidity of change reminds me that every confluence of knowledge is tentative and ephemeral. Despite its commitments to timeless standards of truth, ethics is historical.
